sources.citation: Times of India, 22 Feb 2023, 'Hope floats for Ruga revival as researchers find three speakers of language'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: News report; states Grierson gave a skeleton grammar and that there was 'no proper research till publication of The Ruga Language (ABILAC 2016) by Caroline R Marak'.

sources.citation: Ethnologue (2016, the Internet Archive) entry Ruga [ruh]; OLAC listing for ruh (Dec 2024, the Internet Archive); English Wikipedia 'Ruga language'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonological information; OLAC lists only Glottolog and Ethnologue resources for ruh.

sources.citation: Hyslop, G., L. Konnerth, S. Morey & P. Sarmah (eds.) 2014. North East Indian Linguistics 6; Konnerth et al. (eds.) 2015 NEIL 7; Konnerth et al. (eds.) 2018 NEIL 8. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full-text search: no paper on Ruga and no mention of Ruga (only 'Dibrugarh' string hits).

sources.citation: Hyslop, G., S. Morey & M. W. Post (eds.) 2011/2015. Language and Culture in Northeast India and Beyond: In Honor of Robbins Burling. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. hdl 1885/38458.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full-text search: no mention of Ruga.

sources.citation: Wood, Daniel Cody. 2008. An Initial Reconstruction of Proto-Boro-Garo. MA thesis, University of Oregon. hdl 1794/9485.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ruga appears only in the review of earlier classifications (pp. 3-6); data drawn from Bodo, Garo, Rabha, Deuri grammars; no Ruga data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Burling, Robbins. n.d. [c. 2007]. Language, Ethnicity and Migration in Northeastern India. Ms., personal website (the Internet Archive 2010).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic: Ruga enclave surrounded by Garo, not mutually intelligible with Garo, known only to a handful of older speakers (pp. 9-10); no phonology.

sources.citation: Burling, Robbins. 2006. Change with Continuity in the Boro-Garo Languages. Paper, NEILS Guwahati 2006 (Internet Archive copy of personal-site PDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ruga named once in the list of Boro-Garo languages ('the soon to become extinct Ruga'); nothing on its phonology.

sources.citation: Burling, Robbins. c. 2006. Proto-Boro-Garo Cognate Chart (xls) with Directions (pdf). Personal website (the Internet Archive 2010).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Columns for Tiwa, Boro, Garo, Rabha only; no Ruga data.

sources.citation: Joseph, U. V. & Robbins Burling. 2006. The Comparative Phonology of the Boro-Garo Languages. Mysore: CIIL. p. 2.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ruga mentioned only in the classification overview (moribund, Koch subgroup, close to A'tong and Rabha); Ruga is not one of the four compared languages; nothing on Ruga stress.

sources.citation: Burling, Robbins. 2004. The Language of the Modhupur Mandi (Garo), Vol. I: Grammar. New Delhi: Bibliophile South Asia / U. Michigan spobooks. pp. 11-12.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Garo stress only (ch. 3, already in catalog for garo1247). On Ruga: moribund, Koch subgroup, remaining speakers' Ruga heavily Garo-influenced; no Ruga phonology.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1903. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Part II: Bodo, Naga and Kachin groups. Calcutta. Ruga paragraph pp. 94-95; Ruga column in standard words and sentences pp. 135ff.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives only speaker estimate, location (head-waters of the Kitai), case suffixes (gen. ni/nia, dat. no, abl. nia), plural dika/rung, pronouns, verb tense suffixes; no accent or tone remark for Ruga.

sources.citation: Marak, Caroline R. 2016. The Ruga Language. Guwahati: Anundoram Borooah Institute of Language, Art and Culture (ABILAC). xii+124 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL4001.R84 M37 2016); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL4001.R84 M37 2016
sources.note: The only modern description of Ruga (Glottolog grammar sketch, 136 pp.); its phonology chapter is the one place a first-hand Ruga stress statement can be expected. MPI-EVA/hh holds a scan per the Glottolog record.

sources.citation: Jacquesson, François & Seino van Breugel. 2017. The linguistic reconstruction of the past: The case of the Boro-Garo languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 40(1): 90-122.

sources.note: Comparative Boro-Garo study by the two authors with access to Burling's unpublished Ruga notes; may cite Ruga forms with prosodic marking. HAL halshs-02924911 is a notice without file.

sources.note: PLSI state volumes carry short community-written sketches of minor Garo Hills varieties (Ruga, Atong, Chibok etc.), sometimes with a phonology paragraph; not verified that a Ruga chapter exists.

sources.citation: van Breugel, Seino. 2014. A Grammar of Atong (Brill's Studies in South and Southwest Asian Languages 5). Leiden: Brill. [PhD version: La Trobe 2008, OPAL doi 10.26181/32274687.v1, metadata only]

sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Closest sister language with a full modern grammar; ch. 1-2 discuss Ruga and give the Atong prosodic analysis that a Ruga statement would be compared against; may contain remarks on Burling's Ruga field data.

sources.citation: Burling, Robbins. Unpublished Ruga field notes / word lists (Garo Hills, 1990s-2000s), referred to in Burling 2004: 11-12.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Burling personally interviewed the last Ruga speakers; if his notes are archived (U. Michigan Bentley Library papers or CoRSAL) they would be the only phonetically transcribed Ruga data by a phonologist who described Garo stress.
